title: Discovery of germanium-based hybrid perovskites with high photovoltaic performance with machine-learning.
summary: XGBoost screened a large theoretical candidate set, and learned structure-property models narrowed the shortlist for first-principles evaluation. Four lead-free germanium-based candidates had calculated band gaps in a photovoltaic-relevant range; these are computational predictions, not synthesized materials or measured device performance.
ai_technology: XGBoost screens candidate compositions; learned structure-property models prioritize a shortlist for density-functional-theory evaluation.
organization: Fudan University; East China Normal University; Lynbrook High School

evidence.tested: Four candidate compositions had HSE+SOC-calculated indirect band gaps of approximately 1.17–1.75 eV after screening about 180,000 theoretical candidates.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is computational, with disagreement across learned models and DFT settings; no synthesis or photovoltaic-device performance was reported.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning screening enabled prioritization and computational characterization of specific candidate perovskites.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
